{{Orphan|date=August 2023}}

The '''Survey of Consumer Expectations''' is a monthly survey of U.S. households by the [[New York Federal Reserve Bank]]. The people are asked about how much the expect to spend, how high they expect inflation to be, their employment situation, and whether they are searching for a job.

== Methodology ==
About 4500 consumers have been surveyed each year since 2013.  Survey results are calibrated to be demographically representative of U.S. households.<ref>Olivier Armantier, Giorgio Topa, Wilbert van der Klaauw, and Basit Zafar. [https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/epr/2017/epr_2017_survey-consumer-expectations_armantier.pdf An Overview of the Survey of Consumer Expectations]. ''FRBNY Economic Policy Review''. December 2017</ref>  Monthly survey results and detailed microdata are published at the New York Fed site.<ref>[https://www.newyorkfed.org/press/press-briefing-survey-of-consumer-expectations Press briefing by NY Federal Reserve Bank]. 2016</ref><ref>[https://bankingjournal.aba.com/tag/survey-of-consumer-expectations/ Fed Survey: Consumers’ Spending Expectations Fall]. American Banking Association news item.  8 July 2019.</ref><ref>[https://www.newyorkfed.org/microeconomics/sce Survey of Consumer Expectations, NY Fed monthly report]. Center for Microeconomic Data, NY Federal Reserve Bank.  Includes download links.</ref>

== Results ==
The survey's results are used to make inferences about public [[Inflation#Inflation expectations|expectations of U.S. dollar inflation]].<ref>[https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-fed-consumer-expectations/us-consumer-inflation-expectations-drop-again-new-york-fed-survey-idUSKBN1XF2MV Reuters news for inflation expections of the public]. Reuters.</ref><ref>Derby, Michael S. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/new-york-fed-survey-finds-easing-august-inflation-expectations-11568043239 Inflation Expectations Ease in August, New York Fed Survey Says]. ''Wall Street Journal'', 9 Sept 2019</ref>

The survey has illuminated the degree to which employed workers are offered much higher-wage jobs than the unemployed, even holding constant the observable attributes of the workers.<ref>R. Jason Faberman, Thomas Haasl, Andreas I. Mueller, [[Ayşegül Şahin]], and Giorgio Topa. [https://libertystreeteconomics.newyorkfed.org/2018/04/do-the-employed-get-better-job-offers.html Do the Employed Get Better Job Offers?] Blog post at NY Fed. April 4, 2018.</ref>
